tells.1: none. It reads like real clinic copy, with a rhetorical-question opener and a slightly clunky, repetitive marker list ('to check... to monitor').
tells.2: Tidy, even sentence rhythm and a generic 'helps guide care as your dog ages' clause, but no strong tell.
tells.3: Two em-dashes plus a tacked-on promotional benefit tag ('a practical way to get a fuller picture... make the most of their yearly checkup').
tells.4: none. It is lean and direct; at most, it is a little clipped.
tells.5: A formulaic closing benefit line ('a practical way to get a fuller picture of your dog's health and more out of the checkup') appended to the price.
tells.6: A softer version of the closing benefit-tag pattern ('a simple way to get the full picture'), though the casual voice ('hits 7', 'something's off') feels natural.

reason: Version 4 delivers the recommendation, the reason, the baseline benefit and the price with no filler or salesy add-on, so it reads as credible and professional. Versions 3 and 5 lose credibility to the boilerplate 'fuller picture' closer, and version 1 feels authentic but is wordier and less persuasive.
